t.1.7.1: The Sūta said: Cursed by Bhṛgu, Fire grew angry and then spoke these words: "What is this rash deed, O brahmin, that you have just now done?"
t.1.7.3: For a witness who, when questioned, knowingly gives false testimony would destroy seven of his forebears in his family, and likewise seven of those who come after him.
t.1.7.2: I strive in dharma and speak the truth impartially; when I was questioned, I spoke the truth. What transgression of mine is there in this?
t.1.7.4: And he who knows the true nature of the matter at hand, and, knowing it, does not speak, he too is stained by that very same sin; of this there is no doubt.
t.1.7.6: Having made myself manifold by my yogic power, I abide in many forms: in the agnihotra offerings, in the sattra rites, in the sacred ceremonies, and in the sacrifices.
t.1.7.5: I too am able to curse you, but brāhmaṇas are to be honored by me. And though you know it, I shall tell you plainly; hear it.
t.1.7.7: Whatever oblation is offered into me according to the rite enjoined by the Veda, by that the gods and the ancestors are indeed satisfied.
t.1.7.9: Therefore the gods are the ancestors, and the ancestors too are the gods; on the days of the moon's change they are worshipped both as one and separately.
t.1.7.8: The waters are all the hosts of the gods, and the waters likewise are the hosts of the ancestors; and the new-moon and full-moon rites belong to the gods together with the ancestors.
t.1.7.12: Having reflected, the Fire then withdrew himself from the agnihotras of the twice-born and from the rites of sacrifices and sattras.
t.1.7.10: Since the gods and the ancestors are always offered oblations in me, I am thus known as the mouth of the thirty gods and of the ancestors.
t.1.7.11: On the new-moon day the ancestors, and on the full-moon day the gods, receive offerings through my mouth alone, and they eat the oblation that has been offered. How then shall I, an eater of everything, be their mouth?
t.1.7.13: Then, without Agni, all creatures were deprived of the syllable Om and the vaṣaṭ call, bereft of svadhā and svāhā, and they became deeply distressed.
t.1.7.15: Then the seers and the gods went to Brahmā and reported to him the curse upon Agni and the cessation of the rites.
t.1.7.14: Then the seers, deeply distressed, went to the gods and spoke these words: "Because of the loss of Agni and the cessation of the rites, the three worlds, though blameless, have fallen into confusion. Arrange what must be done in this matter, so that there may be no delay."
t.1.7.16: O greatly fortunate one, Agni was indeed cursed by Bhṛgu for a certain reason; how, being the mouth of the gods and likewise the first eater of the shares of the sacrifice, will the eater of oblations come to be an eater of all things in all the worlds?
t.1.7.17: Having heard those words of theirs, the maker of the worlds summoned Agni, the imperishable one who brings beings into existence, and spoke gentle words to him.
t.1.7.18: You are the maker of all the worlds here, and their end as well; you uphold the three worlds and set the sacred rites in motion. So act, Lord of the worlds, that the rites may not be cut off.
t.1.7.19: Why are you so bewildered, Hutāśana, when you are the lord, since you are the purifier in the world and dwell within all beings?
t.1.7.21: Just as everything touched by the rays of the sun is seen to be pure, so everything burnt by your flames will become pure.
t.1.7.20: You will not become an eater of all things with your whole body; those flames of yours that are at the place of seizing, they will burn everything, O flaming one.
t.1.7.23: "So be it," the fire replied to him, the Grandsire, and he went to carry out the command of the god, the Supreme Lord.
t.1.7.22: Therefore, Agni, you are a mighty splendor that has issued forth from your own power; by your own splendor make that curse of the seer come true, O lord, and receive in your mouth the share of the gods and your own that is offered as oblation.
t.1.7.24: Then the divine seers, delighted, went back the way they had come, and the seers performed all their rites as before.
t.1.7.25: The gods in heaven rejoiced, and so did the hosts of beings of the world; and Agni, his taint destroyed, attained the highest joy.
t.1.7.26: Thus this is the ancient tale that arose from the curse of Agni: the destruction of Puloma and the birth of Cyavana.
